title: The band splits and the Southern Yacht Club contract
summary: Celestin and others tell the Southern Yacht Club he quit; Ridgley goes down, the club cancels them, and he plays with seven pieces.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: When that band split up, who stayed with you? Which ones stayed with you and which ones went with Sillis?

Well, our band, we played at the Temple Roof Garden on a Wednesday night. Sillis Stain, the two Mareros and Paul Baum. They had a morning meeting. See? And the band, that's where they pulled out for me. Well, Lewis Madison, he was out among them and he heard of me. He called me up at 4 o'clock in the morning and he told me what they had done. But they had went out to Southern Yacht Club and told the secretary, Mr. Power and the president, Mr. Gossett, that I had quit playing music and turned everything over to them. That's what Celis Stain did. And so, next morning, I went down to the Southern Yacht headquarters. It was across from Beekman there. They had a...where they used to meet. And so, it was about 11 o'clock. And I got there. Well, Mr. Gossett said to me, well, originally, he said, what are you doing down here? I said, well, I just heard something blowing in the air, Mr. Gossett, and I come down to see about it. So, I heard that, they hired another band. He said, have you quit playing music? I said, no, sir. He said, you didn't quit playing music and turn everything...what did he say? Well, that Henry said Doug, the fella named, used to smoke those cigarettes and go out on the porch all the time. What is the name? Play cornet. I said, Celis Stain. He said, well, he was down there hitting the banjo player and they came down and told us that you had quit playing and turn everything over to them and we brought up a contract with them. Is that so? I told him, no, sir. He said, well, originally, how many of the band had you got? He said, is that girl playing with you? I said, yes, sir. He said, you got a drummer? I said, yes, sir. Well, I think I had a name fired. He said to the sonographer, he said, I want you to write that fellow Celis Stain a letter and tell him not to show up on the job Wednesday night. Because we have made that different arrangement with a different band. And then he wrote him that letter and he wrote me and he said, Ridley, say, you be out Wednesday night. Whoever you got, say, you bring them. So I went out and I had seven pieces and we went out and we did pretty good, but I know not that they had the band.
